text:
Both halves of the report are addressed on branch `fix/files-upload-retry` (3 commits, full test suite green).

**Why their uploads didn't retry:** it wasn't the retry policy — 429s retry for any HTTP method as long as the body can be resent. The problem was body replay. `Raw.Do` hands the reader to `http.NewRequestWithContext`, which only wires up `GetBody` (the replay hook the retry transport needs) for in-memory readers like `*bytes.Reader`. A body streamed from `os.Open` had no `GetBody`, so the retry transport treated it as non-replayable and returned the first 429 immediately. Their other calls worked because JSON bodies are encoded into a `bytes.Reader`. `RetryAllMethods: true` never mattered here — it only gates 502/503/504.

**The fix** (`pipedrive/raw.go:130`, `enableBodyReplay`): when a body implements `io.Seeker` and has no `GetBody`, `Raw.Do` now records the reader's current offset, rewinds to it for every retry attempt, and sets an explicit `Content-Length` from the seeker. The reader is wrapped in `io.NopCloser` so the transport's per-attempt close can't close the caller's file mid-retry — which means `Raw.Do` no longer closes seekable bodies at all; callers own their readers (the normal `defer f.Close()` pattern is unaffected, and this is flagged under "Changed" in the changelog). Non-seekable streams keep the old fail-fast behavior, now documented on `Files.Add`.

**The ergonomics fix:** new `Files.Upload(ctx, fileName, reader, opts...)` in `pipedrive/v1/files.go`, mirroring `CallLogs.AddRecording`. It builds the multipart body via the shared `internal/multipartbody` helper (extended with `NewFileWithFields`), and the new `WithFilesFormFields(url.Values)` option carries the `deal_id`/`person_id`/etc. association fields that `POST /files` accepts as form fields. Since the encoded body is a `*bytes.Reader`, uploads through `Upload` retry safely regardless of the input reader.
